description: Spacecraft thermal control subsystem fault knowledge base for anomaly explanation and solution retrieval.

faults.name: Overheating / Loss of Radiator Heat Rejection
faults.telemetry_signature: Sustained upward drift in a temperature channel beyond the normal operating band, often a slow contextual anomaly that accelerates rather than a single spike.
likely_causes: Degraded radiator surface (optical/thermal coating breakdown) reducing heat rejection to deep space
Failure or blockage in a fluid loop or heat pipe carrying heat to the radiator
Increased internal heat generation from a subsystem operating outside its planned duty cycle
recommended_actions: Reduce duty cycle or power on non-essential heat-generating components
Check fluid loop / heat pipe telemetry (pressure, flow) for a mechanical root cause
If sustained, command safe mode to protect temperature-sensitive components until root cause is identified

real_world_example.summary: Multi-layer insulation blankets and radiators protect against overheating while retaining heat to prevent excess cooling; components can cease functioning if temperatures exceed narrow operating ranges, making thermal fault protection essential alongside power and attitude protection.
real_world_example.source: Fault Protection Techniques in JPL Spacecraft, P. Morgan

faults.name: Under-Temperature / Heater Failure
faults.telemetry_signature: Sustained downward drift in a temperature channel below the safe operating band, typically a slow contextual anomaly following loss of active heating or loss of sun exposure.
likely_causes: Failure of a thermostatically-controlled resistive heater
Loss of solar exposure due to an attitude/pointing anomaly
Propellant or fluid freezing following a power/attitude cascading failure
recommended_actions: Verify heater command/status telemetry to confirm heater is receiving power and responding
Cross-check with attitude and power telemetry for a cascading root cause
Prioritize restoring sun-pointing or heater power before the affected component drops below its qualified low-temperature limit

real_world_example.summary: After a 1991 tumble anomaly, Olympus's batteries discharged, the satellite cooled down, and its propellant froze - illustrating how a cascading attitude/power failure can rapidly produce a severe under-temperature condition.
real_world_example.source: AEROSPACE REPORT NO. TOR-2009(8591)-14, Effective Fault Management Guidelines

faults.name: Fluid Loop / Heat Pipe Degradation
faults.telemetry_signature: Gradual reduction in heat transport efficiency visible as slowly widening temperature differential between two related channels (e.g. source vs. radiator) - a contextual, multi-channel anomaly.
likely_causes: Reliability shortfall in pumped fluid loops or loop heat pipes versus design expectations
Working fluid depletion or blockage within a variable/axially-grooved heat pipe
Long-duration wear exceeding conservative design-phase reliability estimates
recommended_actions: Track the temperature differential trend across the loop rather than a single sensor in isolation
Reduce load on the affected loop and redistribute heat-generating tasks if redundancy exists
Flag for ground engineering review; fluid loop issues are rarely correctable via autonomous action alone

real_world_example.mission: Communications Technology Satellite (1977) and related fluidic TCS studies
real_world_example.summary: A review of fluidic thermal control technologies (pumped fluid loops, loop heat pipes, variable/axially-grooved heat pipes) found reliability is frequently overestimated at the design phase, leading to higher in-flight failure rates than intended.
real_world_example.source: Spacecraft Fluidic Thermal Control Subsystem Reliability, DTIC

faults.name: Thermal-Induced Safe Mode Entry
faults.telemetry_signature: Temperature channel crosses a predefined safety threshold immediately followed by broad changes across many other channels (non-essential systems shutting down) - a sharp point anomaly triggering a system-wide state change.
likely_causes: Autonomous fault protection responding to an out-of-range thermal reading
Cascading effect from an upstream attitude or power anomaly removing active thermal control
Cosmic-ray-induced false trigger signal misread as a genuine thermal fault
recommended_actions: Confirm whether the temperature reading itself is valid or a false trigger (check for corresponding attitude/power anomalies)
Follow standard safe-mode recovery procedure: verify essential systems (thermal, comms, attitude) are stable before re-enabling other subsystems
Review fault-protection trigger thresholds if false triggers recur

real_world_example.summary: Safe mode shuts down all non-essential systems, retaining only thermal management, radio reception, and attitude control, and is triggered automatically when telemetry crosses predefined dangerous thresholds - including, in some cases, false triggers from cosmic rays striking onboard electronics.

faults.name: Multi-Layer Insulation (MLI) Degradation
faults.telemetry_signature: Slow upward drift in baseline temperature of an externally-facing component with increasing sensitivity to sun angle - a contextual anomaly correlated with orbital sun-exposure geometry.
likely_causes: MLI blanket material degradation from prolonged UV/thermal cycling exposure
Micrometeoroid or debris damage puncturing insulation
Outgassing-related property change in the insulation material
recommended_actions: Trend temperature against sun-angle telemetry to confirm the exposure correlation
Adjust attitude/pointing to reduce direct exposure of the affected area if operationally possible
Factor accelerated degradation into long-term thermal budget planning

faults.name: Louver Actuator Stiction
faults.telemetry_signature: Louver position telemetry stops responding proportionally to commanded thermal control changes - a point anomaly where the mechanism sticks at a fixed position despite changing thermal demand.
likely_causes: Mechanical stiction in the bimetallic or motor-driven actuator
Lubricant degradation in the actuator mechanism
Debris or thermal distortion binding the louver blades
recommended_actions: Command a full-range exercise cycle to attempt to free the stuck mechanism
Cross-check whether the louver is stuck open (overheating risk) or stuck closed (undercooling risk) to prioritize response
Compensate via heater/duty-cycle adjustment on affected components if the mechanism cannot be freed

faults.name: Heater Duty Cycle Anomaly
faults.telemetry_signature: Heater on/off cycling frequency or duration deviates from the expected pattern for current thermal conditions - a contextual anomaly in commanded-vs-actual heater behavior.
likely_causes: Thermostat setpoint drift
Heater element partial degradation requiring longer on-time to reach setpoint
Thermal control software logic fault
recommended_actions: Compare heater duty cycle trend against the temperature it's meant to control
Verify thermostat setpoint configuration hasn't drifted from intended values
Check for a software/logic fault if duty cycle behavior doesn't match the temperature trend at all

faults.name: Radiator Coating Degradation (Optical Property Shift)
faults.telemetry_signature: Baseline operating temperature slowly rises across many orbits with no corresponding change in internal heat generation - a slow contextual anomaly best seen in long-duration trend data.
likely_causes: Atomic oxygen erosion of radiator surface coating (common in low Earth orbit)
UV-induced degradation of thermal control coating
Contamination deposit on the radiator surface reducing emissivity
recommended_actions: Trend baseline temperature over the full mission to characterize the degradation rate
Factor coating degradation into long-term thermal margin planning
Cross-check against known atomic-oxygen/UV exposure models for the orbit

faults.name: Thermal Sensor Calibration Drift
faults.telemetry_signature: One temperature sensor slowly diverges from a redundant or co-located sensor reading the same physical location - a slow contextual anomaly isolated to sensor data quality rather than the actual thermal environment.
likely_causes: Sensor calibration drift over mission lifetime
Radiation-induced sensor reading error
Connector/wiring degradation affecting sensor signal integrity
recommended_actions: Cross-check against a redundant or nearby sensor before trusting the reading
Apply a calibration offset correction if drift is consistent and well-characterized
Flag the sensor as degraded rather than assuming a real thermal event if only one sensor shows the drift

faults.name: Cryocooler Performance Degradation
faults.telemetry_signature: Cooled instrument/detector temperature slowly rises despite constant cryocooler commanded power - a contextual anomaly in cooling efficiency rather than a sudden failure.
likely_causes: Mechanical wear in the cryocooler compressor over mission lifetime
Contamination buildup reducing heat exchanger efficiency
Vibration-induced performance degradation
recommended_actions: Trend cooling efficiency (temperature achieved per unit power) over time
Check for a correlation with recent mechanical/vibration events
Adjust instrument duty cycle to reduce heat load if efficiency continues declining

faults.name: Thermal Cycling Fatigue Crack
faults.telemetry_signature: Sudden, discrete step-change in a structural or joint temperature reading - a point anomaly that may recur intermittently as the crack opens/closes with thermal expansion.
likely_causes: Repeated thermal expansion/contraction cycling fatiguing a structural joint or thermal strap connection
Material fatigue at a mechanical interface exceeding design cycle life
Vibration-induced crack propagation
recommended_actions: Document the intermittent pattern; a recurring step-change is a strong fatigue-crack indicator
Avoid unnecessary additional thermal cycling of the affected area if operationally possible
Flag for structural/mechanical engineering review

faults.name: Solar Array Thermal Gradient Anomaly
faults.telemetry_signature: Uneven temperature distribution across solar array panels beyond what sun angle alone would predict - a contextual anomaly visible when comparing multiple array temperature sensors.
likely_causes: Partial shadowing from a deployed structure or another spacecraft component
Localized cell/panel degradation changing thermal-optical properties
Array not fully deployed or slightly misaligned from expected orientation
recommended_actions: Cross-check against deployment-status and attitude telemetry for a shadowing or misalignment explanation
Compare against power output telemetry from the same panel region
Flag for review if the gradient doesn't correlate with any known geometric cause

faults.name: Propellant Line Freeze Risk
faults.telemetry_signature: Propellant line temperature approaches the freezing point of the propellant - a slow contextual anomaly, often following an extended eclipse or a heater fault upstream.
likely_causes: Heater failure on the propellant line
Extended eclipse duration exceeding thermal design margin
Reduced power availability limiting heater operation
recommended_actions: Prioritize heater power allocation to propellant lines if power is constrained
Verify heater command/status telemetry for the affected line
Avoid commanding propulsion system use until temperature is confirmed safely above freezing

faults.name: Battery Compartment Thermal Runaway Precursor
faults.telemetry_signature: Rapid, accelerating temperature rise in the battery compartment distinct from normal charge/discharge heating - an early-stage point anomaly that, if uncaught, can cascade into the battery thermal runaway fault.
likely_causes: Developing internal cell fault generating excess heat
Compartment cooling/heat-rejection path partially blocked
Charge control fault causing sustained overcharge heating
recommended_actions: Cross-reference with the battery-side thermal-runaway and overcharge checks immediately - this is an early warning for both
Reduce or suspend charging on the affected compartment as a precaution
Treat as time-critical; escalate faster than a typical slow-drift thermal anomaly

faults.name: Instrument Detector Temperature Excursion
faults.telemetry_signature: Science instrument detector temperature briefly exceeds its stability requirement without exceeding safety limits - a point anomaly affecting data quality rather than hardware safety.
likely_causes: Brief attitude maneuver changing sun exposure to the instrument
Nearby subsystem operating in an unusually high-power mode
Cooling system transient during a mode transition
recommended_actions: Flag affected science data collected during the excursion window for quality review
Cross-check against attitude and power-mode telemetry for a timing correlation
Consider operational constraints to avoid recurrence during critical observations

faults.name: Eclipse Transition Thermal Shock
faults.telemetry_signature: Rapid temperature change rate (not just magnitude) at eclipse entry/exit exceeding the expected rate-of-change envelope - a point anomaly defined by rate rather than absolute temperature.
likely_causes: Faster-than-nominal eclipse transition due to orbital geometry
Reduced thermal mass/insulation at the affected location increasing sensitivity to rapid change
Component operating closer to a rate-of-change design limit than expected
recommended_actions: Compare observed rate-of-change against component qualification limits, not just absolute temperature
Review orbital geometry for any recent change affecting eclipse transition speed
Consider pre-emptive heater adjustment ahead of predicted fast transitions

faults.name: Heat Pipe Non-Condensable Gas Accumulation
faults.telemetry_signature: Gradual reduction in heat pipe transport efficiency with a growing 'dead zone' temperature gradient near one end - a slow contextual anomaly visible in the temperature differential along the pipe's length.
likely_causes: Non-condensable gas generation from internal material outgassing over mission lifetime
Working fluid degradation producing gas byproducts
Manufacturing-origin gas trapped in the pipe slowly expanding effect over time
recommended_actions: Trend the temperature gradient along the heat pipe length to characterize the growing dead zone
Redistribute heat load away from the affected pipe if redundancy exists
Factor reduced heat transport capacity into thermal margin planning

faults.name: Thermal Coating Contamination from Outgassing
faults.telemetry_signature: Slow baseline temperature drift beginning early in the mission and gradually leveling off - a contextual anomaly with a characteristic decelerating-drift shape distinct from ongoing degradation.
likely_causes: Volatile materials outgassing from spacecraft components depositing contamination on thermal control surfaces
Contamination redistributing and settling on radiators/sensors over the early mission phase
recommended_actions: Compare drift timing against known outgassing timelines (typically most active early in mission)
Distinguish from ongoing degradation faults by checking whether the drift is leveling off rather than continuing to accelerate
No corrective action usually needed beyond updated thermal margin bookkeeping if the drift has stabilized

faults.name: Payload Duty-Cycle-Driven Overheating
faults.telemetry_signature: Temperature rise directly tracks an increase in payload/instrument operating duty cycle - a contextual anomaly explainable by a usage-pattern change rather than a hardware fault.
likely_causes: Mission operations increased instrument duty cycle beyond original thermal design assumptions
Extended observation campaign exceeding planned thermal recovery time between operations
recommended_actions: Cross-check temperature rise timing directly against commanded duty-cycle changes before assuming a hardware fault
Adjust operational duty cycle or add recovery/cooldown periods between observations
Update thermal models if the new duty cycle is intended to be sustained

faults.name: Passive Radiator Blockage
faults.telemetry_signature: Sudden step increase in baseline temperature coincident with a deployment or attitude-change event - a point anomaly tied to a specific event that altered the radiator's view to space.
likely_causes: A deployable structure (antenna, array, boom) now partially obstructing the radiator's view to deep space
Attitude change altering the radiator's effective heat-rejection geometry
Debris or ice buildup on the radiator surface
recommended_actions: Cross-check against deployment and attitude event logs for a timing correlation
Assess whether an alternate attitude profile can restore radiator view to space
If a deployable is the obstruction, evaluate whether it can be repositioned
